holidays.name: National Spaghetti Day
holidays.description: A day to twirl, slurp and sauce your way through a big plate of pasta. Spaghetti is cheap, comforting and endlessly customizable, so it works for a fancy dinner or a college-dorm meal.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its founder is unclear, but it has been marked on January 4 for years as a pasta lover's excuse to eat well.
holidays.funFact: The word spaghetti is the plural of 'spaghetto,' which means 'little string' in Italian.

holidays.name: National Trivia Day
holidays.description: A day for useless-but-delightful facts. Quiz your friends, host a pub-style trivia night, or fall down an internet rabbit hole about the migration of the Arctic tern.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. It falls at the start of the year, which makes it a good time to start collecting new facts.
holidays.funFact: The word 'trivia' comes from the Latin 'trivium,' meaning 'three roads.' It referred to a place where roads met, where everyday gossip was swapped.

holidays.name: Dimpled Chad Day
holidays.description: A tribute to one of the most famous bits of paper confetti in political history. It is for anyone who has squinted at a ballot and wondered whether a tiny dent counts as a vote.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that nods to the 2000 U.S. presidential election recount. In that recount, election workers closely inspected punch-card ballots for hanging, pregnant and dimpled chads.
holidays.funFact: A 'chad' is the tiny scrap of paper punched out of a ballot card. After the 2000 recount, the word became a household term almost overnight.
